questions.q: Which encoding is the safe default for a NOMINAL column such as city?
questions.explain: One-hot creates a separate 0/1 column per category, so no false order is implied.

questions.q: For an ORDINAL column with values basic, standard and premium, what should you do with OrdinalEncoder?
options: Let it choose the order automatically
Pass the categories in their true order explicitly
Use one-hot instead in every case
questions.explain: By default the encoder orders categories alphabetically, which would put premium before standard. State the true order with the categories argument.

questions.q: What does handle_unknown="ignore" do in OneHotEncoder?
options: Fits on the test set as well
Encodes a category unseen during fit as all zeros instead of raising an error
questions.explain: New data will eventually contain categories the encoder never saw. This setting keeps transform from crashing.

questions.q: In the lesson's experiment, why did city numbered 0, 1, 2 give an R-squared of only 0.04?
options: A linear model can only draw a straight line through the codes, but Boston (the middle code) spends the most
questions.explain: The fake ordering forces a straight-line relationship, so a middle category cannot sit above both neighbors. One-hot gives each city its own level.

questions.q: Where should an encoder such as OneHotEncoder be fitted?
options: On the full dataset before splitting
On the training set only, then used to transform validation and test
questions.explain: Encoders learn categories from data, so like any learned preprocessing step they must be fitted on training data only to avoid leakage.
